cells.tense: Right now, the quiet in you is being kept on purpose and it is holding.
cells.ask: Spend one conversation listening past the point where you'd usually start forming your reply. Let them finish before you speak.
cells.core:
Nothing is being argued in you tonight. That's the whole of it. Your mind is set down, and it stays set down even with another person in the room, which is harder than it sounds. You can hear them without rehearsing an answer, and the hearing isn't costing you anything.

What keeps this going is smaller than it looks. You stay yourself while you feel with someone, and you keep making the little calls that hold it there — when to speak, when to wait, where you stop being fully available and don't resent it. Staying calm around another person gets remade in each conversation. What keeps it is the same thing that built it.
cells.sheetLine: Your quiet is being kept on purpose, and it holds.
cells.verb: Resting the mind into accurate quiet
cells.place: Where two people meet and stay distinct

cells.tense: You are already in a conversation that hasn't happened, bracing for how it will go.
cells.ask: Pick the conversation you keep running in your head. Set it down, and don't decide anything until the real one starts.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead of you is a conversation you have already had several times, in your head, and it keeps ending badly. You're in it now, running lines, checking for the exit early. The quiet you were resting in has turned into preparation.

What you're protecting matters, and the effort is real. But you're paying now for something that may not arrive, and the person in front of you today gets the version of you that is already partway out the door. Nothing has gone wrong yet, and you're using tomorrow's calm to get through a day that hasn't asked for it. Put it down, and let the real one start.
cells.sheetLine: You're spending tomorrow's calm on a conversation that hasn't happened.

cells.tense: You are with people these days without quite being with them.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you actually felt today. Not the summary — the thing itself, out loud, once.
cells.core:
The space around you with people has gone quiet in a way that isn't peace. You're there in body and somewhere else in the rest of you, and you've been calling that being tired. You don't much wonder how someone's day went lately. When a voice goes flat across from you, you hear it and it doesn't move you.

The ability to feel with people hasn't gone anywhere. What's gone quiet is the pull toward them, and it comes back on its own schedule. It doesn't come back by forcing yourself into closeness. Leave a little room for it today, and don't push yourself into feeling something that isn't there yet.

cells.tense: You are already reading people well, and you keep talking about it like it is nothing much.
cells.ask: Next time someone says you understood, don't wave it off. Say thank you, once, and stop there.
cells.core:
You catch things about people without trying to. The shift in someone's voice before they say what's wrong. The thing they aren't saying. You adjust how you talk to them and don't notice you did it, and you'd call it just paying attention. When it's going well, someone leaves a conversation with you feeling more like themselves and neither of you names why.

That skill is yours, and you've been crediting the situation instead of yourself. Saying so isn't a brag — you're the one who learned it, one conversation at a time, and it works because it's real. Once you count it as yours, you get to choose where it goes instead of it choosing for you.
cells.sheetLine: You're reading people well and calling it the situation.
